Notable mappings: merchant names (CVS Pharmacy, Chipotle, Whole Foods, Shell, Starbucks, Uber, Spotify, Netflix, Amazon, Target) were mapped to their transaction categories (Pharmacy, Restaurants & bars, Groceries, Gas, Coffee shops, Taxi & ride shares, Music & audio, Movies & TV, Retail). Broader categories like "Food & drink", "Transportation", "Entertainment", "Shopping", "Housing & utilities", "Health & wellness" were mapped to their closest detailed counterpart as "Other" when they appeared as primary values.
plan.amount_transform_reasoning: The sample amounts show one positive value (3200.0) and nine negative values (-87.43, -6.75, -42.5, -15.99, -58.2, -45.0, -110.0, -23.18, -18.5). The positive value is consistent with income (Direct Deposit Payroll at $3200), while the negative values are consistent with expenses (groceries, rides, entertainment, utilities). This matches the 'expense_negative' convention where expenses are negative numbers and income is positive — no transformation needed.

plan.category_map_reasoning: All category values are legitimate spending or income categories. Merchant names like CVS Pharmacy, Whole Foods Market, and Amazon.com are mapped to their primary merchant categories (Retail for general retailers, Groceries for Whole Foods, etc.). Generic categories like "Transportation," "Housing," "Shopping," "Entertainment," "Health," and "Utilities" are mapped to their corresponding Budgy primary categories with reasonable detailed categories. Specific merchant categories are mapped with more specificity: Shell and Uber for transportation, Netflix and Spotify for entertainment, Payroll Direct Deposit for income wages, etc. "Payments" is mapped broadly to Transfers > Other transfers due to ambiguity without additional context.
plan.amount_transform_reasoning: The sample Amount (USD) values are all positive numbers (3200.0, 87.43, 6.75, 42.5, 15.99, 58.2, 45.0, 110.0, 23.18, 18.5). Given that the CSV contains both expense categories (Planet Fitness, Shell Gas Station, Chipotle, Netflix, Rent, etc.) and at least one income category (Payroll Direct Deposit at 3200.0), and all amounts are positive, this suggests the CSV uses the standard 'expense_negative' convention where expenses would be stored as negative values. However, since ALL sample values are positive, there is some ambiguity. The 3200.0 value aligned with "Payroll Direct Deposit" (income) being positive is the strongest signal, suggesting this CSV may actually use 'expense_positive' convention (expenses positive, income negative), but more typically positive values in the presence of mixed transaction types indicates standard 'expense_negative' convention with the understanding that expenses should be negated on import if they are currently positive. Recommend reviewing actual transaction signs during import—if expenses are appearing as positive, switch to 'expense_positive'.
